differences.what: roof: the engraving's mansard, its steep lower faces bowed a little to a curb about 2.9 m over the cornice, under a low upper hip; the build's was a 30-degree tin hip
wall head: the engraving's cornice stands about 8.2 m over grade (its soffit 7.9 m); the build's walls stood 0.7 m higher

north pavilion: the north 3.75 m of the front (v 7.5-11.25) is a pavilion standing a little proud, with two round-headed windows a storey under moulded hoods and a light corner strip at its north corner; the build's front is flat there and carries the canted bay
crown: over the pavilion a taller bell-curved mansard with one round-headed dormer, rising about 0.7 m over the main curb; the build has none
corner strip: the engraving draws a light strip down the pavilion's north corner, a stone or painted quoin; T-2404's pavilion turns that corner in its own brick
dormers: round-headed dormers in the mansard's lower face, two seen on the north face; the build's mansard has none

bay window: a one-storey canted bay on the SOUTH part of the front, its front's edges at x 437 and 488 px and its north cheek's foot at 512 px (v 1.54-4.64, 0.58 m out), two round-headed lights in its front, under a flared hood on a console at each corner of its front with a row of modillions; built so by T-2408 (k08.bay.canted_hooded), its edges landing at x 440 and 492 px. The picture's finial is the foot of the upper window that stands on the hood's top, and is not a finial

windows: round-headed sash under moulded hoods on the street front; an upper window over the bay with an ornate head; the north wall's windows flat-headed, two a storey toward the front; the build's are flat-headed two-over-two under segmental brick arches, three on the north wall

entrance: the door at about v 5-6.6 under a hood, reached by a stoop rising north along the front to a porch with a turned balustrade before the pavilion; T-2408 moved the build's door to v 5.8, beside the bay; its hood, the stoop's turn and the porch are still a straight stoop with no hood (T-2409)

fence: a lattice of interlaced pointed arches on a solid base along the street line, and from about x 670 px (v 12.6 on the street line) a close-boarded fence that turns at the north lot line and runs back along it; built so by T-2414 (k11.fence.lattice_arcade, arches three bays of 0.3 m wide, on the kit's curb, then k11.fence.side_boards 1.5 m high), the boards taking over at x 668 px

chimney: a tall stack at the front of the north wall, rising from the cornice beside the crown, its lit east face at x 703-722 px and its north face to 730 px; built so by T-2414, a 0.75 by 0.6 m stack standing on the cornice astride the north wall line (centre u 15.935, v 11.5), projecting to 703.5, 721.6 and 730.0 px, its cap at 12.5 m (y 175 px); the build's second ridge stack over the front half, where the engraving draws sky over the crown, is gone

roof covering: the lower faces and the crown's read as slate in courses; built so by T-2414 (K04 Pennsylvania slate on every face steeper than 45 degrees, the low upper hip, which the picture cannot see, staying tin)

bay window's heights: the engraving draws the bay's sills about 0.4 m over grade and its eaves level with the pavilion's lower window heads, about 0.75 m lower than the build's, on the low principal floor it draws everywhere; the build stands the bay on the house's reconstructed 1.4 m principal floor
bay window's tone: the engraving draws the bay dark against the light front (the hood's shadow, or a painted timber bay); built in the house's brick
bay window's terrace: a low balustrade runs before the bay at its foot; the build has none (T-2409's porch)

board fence's line: the engraving draws the boards' top and foot almost level from x 670 to 990 px, where through its camera a fence running back along the lot line falls toward the horizon; the build's falls as the camera says (the engraving's vertical datum, T-2415)

walls' tone: the engraving draws the front light and the north wall and the pavilion's north half dark, its light from the south-east; the house's colour (the Inter Ocean's 'olive green' of 1887) and its walling are not shown in a monochrome print
the south side wall and the rear: the engraving sees neither
